bib.title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2020

question: How can a large BERT be distilled into a much smaller Transformer student that keeps most of its accuracy on NLU tasks?
hypothesis: Distilling attention matrices, hidden states, embeddings and logits at both pre-training and task-specific stages (with data augmentation) transfers general and task knowledge better than prior BERT distillation.
contributions: A new Transformer distillation method (attention, hidden-state, embedding and prediction-layer losses)
A two-stage framework: general distillation then task-specific distillation with data augmentation
TinyBERT4 reaches over 96.8% of BERT-base on GLUE, 7.5x smaller and 9.4x faster, beating 4-layer baselines
TinyBERT6 performs on par with BERT-base on GLUE

method.summary: Student Transformer (4 or 6 layers) learns to match teacher BERT-base's embeddings, per-layer attention matrices and hidden states (via learned projection), and logits. General distillation on Wikipedia from pre-trained BERT initialises the student; task-specific distillation then runs on a word-replacement-augmented task set with the fine-tuned BERT as teacher.
method.task: knowledge distillation of BERT for GLUE and SQuAD

datasets.name: GLUE (CoLA, SST-2, MRPC, STS-B, QQP, MNLI, QNLI, RTE, WNLI)
datasets.size: CoLA 8.5k, MNLI 393k, MRPC 3.7k, QNLI 105k, QQP 364k, RTE 2.5k, SST-2 67k, STS-B 5.7k train (Table 5 header)
datasets.split: test via official GLUE server (Table 1); dev for ablations
datasets.preprocessing: augmented by Na=20 samples per example; max len 64 single-sentence, 128 pair tasks; STS-B uses original train set for prediction-layer stage

datasets.name: SQuAD v1.1 and v2.0
datasets.preprocessing: prediction-layer distillation on original training set, not augmented

models.name: BERT-TINY, BERT-SMALL, BERT4-PKD, DistilBERT4/6, BERT6-PKD, PD, MobileBERT-TINY

training.objective: sum over layers of lambda_m * L_layer: MSE on embeddings, MSE on hidden states (with projection Wh) plus MSE on unnormalised attention matrices per head, soft cross-entropy on logits (t=1); no prediction-layer loss in general distillation
training.lr: general: as BERT pre-training (not stated); task intermediate-layer 5e-5; prediction-layer from {1e-5,2e-5,3e-5} chosen on dev
training.epochs: general 3; task intermediate-layer 20 (10 for MNLI, QQP, QNLI; 50 for CoLA); prediction-layer 3
training.seq_len: 128 general; 64 single-sentence / 128 pair in task stage
training.hardware: inference speed measured on single NVIDIA K80 GPU; training hardware not stated

other.data_augmentation: pt=0.4, Na=20, K=15; BERT MLM candidates for single-piece words, GloVe neighbours for multi-piece words

inference.samples: single run per setting; seeds not stated

metrics.name: GLUE task metrics (Acc, F1, Matthews corr, Pearson/Spearman)
metrics.definition: as in GLUE paper; Avg is the mean over tasks in Table 1

eval.protocol: Test: official GLUE server, single-task models. Ablations on dev. 4-layer baselines retrained with released code and suggested hyperparameters; 6-layer baselines use reported numbers or released models.

evidence.quote: We set pt = 0.4, Na = 20, K = 15 for all
